name: When is it time to replace porcelain tile instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When is it time to replace porcelain tile instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing your tile floor if you notice widespread hollow sounds beneath tiles, recurring cracked tiles, crumbling grout lines, or signs of moisture damage beneath the floorboards. While single cracked tiles can sometimes be chiseled out and replaced, widespread cracking often signals underlying subfloor flex, improper mortar coverage, or water intrusion. In bathrooms and kitchens, persistent movement or loose tiles will break the water barrier, risking structural rot. If the subfloor has shifted or multiple sections are loose, full replacement provides a secure foundation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace tile when multiple tiles crack, sound hollow, loosen from the subfloor, or show signs of underlying water damage and structural flexing.
